title: Week in Orbit
summary: This week, the space industry is buzzing with partnerships and launches, while defense tech continues to eye the IPO horizon. Meanwhile, budget allocations hint at a growing appetite for resilience in space operations.

themes.title: Partnerships in Connectivity
themes.body: Leaf Space's collaboration with D-Orbit and EnduroSat signifies a push towards enhancing connectivity services in orbit. This trend reflects a broader industry shift towards integrated solutions as satellite constellations proliferate.

themes.title: Budget Boost for Space Resilience
themes.body: The recent $1.4 billion increase in the FY27 budget for space resilience underscores the Pentagon's commitment to safeguarding its assets in an increasingly contested environment. Expect more funding to flow into technologies that enhance operational security.

themes.title: Ariane 6 and Amazon's Ambitions
themes.body: The upcoming Ariane 6 launch, set to deploy 36 Amazon Leo satellites, showcases the competitive landscape of satellite internet. With upgraded boosters in play, this launch could set the stage for Amazon's serious entry into the space-based broadband market.

themes.title: Hypersonics: A Slippery Slope
themes.body: The repeated delays in hypersonic glide-vehicle tests highlight the challenges facing this cutting-edge technology. As the third consecutive slip raises eyebrows, the pressure mounts to deliver on promises that could redefine military capabilities.
